source.text: Καὶ μεθ’ ἡμέρας ἓξ παραλαμβάνει ὁ Ἰησοῦς τὸν Πέτρον καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀναφέρει αὐτοὺς εἰς ὄρος ὑψηλὸν κατ’ ἰδίαν.

records.literal_gloss: And after days six takes along the Jesus the Peter and James and John the brother of him, and brings up them into a mountain high by themselves.

en.L: And after six days Jesus takes along Peter and James and John his brother, and brings them up onto a high mountain by themselves.
en.B: Six days later Jesus took Peter and James and James's brother John with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and led them up a high mountain, where they were alone.
en.R: Six days later, Jesus took Peter, James, and John with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. John was James's brother. Jesus led them up a high mountain. No one else was with them.

decisions.choice: after six days: counted from the sayings of 16:21-28; it may also recall Moses on Mount Sinai
decisions.reason: Matthew rarely gives exact times. In Exodus 24:16 the cloud covered Sinai for six days before God called Moses out of the cloud. With the cloud and the voice in 17:5, the echo may be intended.

decisions.choice: a high mountain: Matthew does not name it
decisions.reason: Later tradition named Mount Tabor in Galilee. Mount Hermon lies near Caesarea Philippi, where the last scene took place (16:13). Matthew leaves it unnamed.

decisions.choice: by themselves: privately, only Jesus and the three
decisions.reason: The phrase means apart from others. The three disciples alone see what follows (compare 26:37).

decisions.choice: takes along, brings up: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: James's brother John (B); John was James's brother (R)
decisions.reason: "His" could be taken as Jesus's brother; Balanced and Readable say that John was the brother of James.

source.text: καὶ μετεμορφώθη ἔμπροσθεν αὐτῶν, καὶ ἔλαμψεν τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ ὡς ὁ ἥλιος, τὰ δὲ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο λευκὰ ὡς τὸ φῶς.

records.literal_gloss: And he was transfigured before them, and shone the face of him as the sun, the and garments of him became white as the light.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was transfigured before them, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face shone like the sun, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothes became white as the light.
en.B: There, before their eyes, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was transfigured. His face shone like the sun, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothes turned white as light.
en.R: While they watched, Jesus was changed. His face shone like the sun. His clothes became as white as light.

decisions.choice: transfigured: his form was changed so that a heavenly glory showed
alternatives: he only looked different in the light
decisions.reason: The verb means to change form. Paul uses it of believers being changed into the Lord's likeness (2 Corinthians 3:18). Matthew describes both Jesus's face and his clothes.

decisions.choice: was transfigured: a passive; God is the one who changed him
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the actor unnamed, a common way of speaking of God's action.

decisions.choice: his face shone like the sun: the glory of God's presence
decisions.reason: Moses' face shone after he had spoken with God on the mountain (Exodus 34:29-35). Jesus has said that the righteous will shine like the sun in their Father's kingdom (13:43; Daniel 12:3). White clothing marks heavenly beings (Daniel 7:9; compare the angel in 28:3).

decisions.choice: transfigured (L, B); changed (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the word long used for this event, as in Mark 9:2. Readable says what it means.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus to begin the scene.

source.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ ὤφθη αὐτοῖς Μωϋσῆς καὶ Ἠλίας συλλαλοῦντες μετ’ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And behold, appeared to them Moses and Elijah talking with him.

en.L: And look, Moses and Elijah appeared to them, talking with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Suddenly Moses and Elijah appeared before them, talking with Jesus.
en.R: All at once Moses and Elijah were there with them, talking with Jesus.

decisions.choice: Moses and Elijah: the law and the prophets, and two men who met God on a mountain
alternatives: two prophets with no special meaning
decisions.reason: Moses gave the law and Elijah stands for the prophets (compare 5:17; 7:12). Both heard God on Sinai, also called Horeb (Exodus 24:12-18; 1 Kings 19:8-18). Elijah was taken up into heaven (2 Kings 2:11), and Malachi said he would come again (Malachi 4:5).

decisions.choice: appeared to them: the disciples saw them
decisions.reason: "To them" means the three disciples. They saw Moses and Elijah and heard them speaking with Jesus.

decisions.choice: look (L); suddenly (B); all at once (R) (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus, since three men are now on the scene.

source.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ· Κύριε, καλόν ἐστιν ἡμᾶς ὧδε εἶναι· εἰ θέλεις, ποιήσω ὧδε τρεῖς σκηνάς, σοὶ μίαν καὶ Μωϋσεῖ μίαν καὶ Ἠλίᾳ μίαν.

records.literal_gloss: Answering and the Peter said to the Jesus, Lord, good it is for us here to be; if you want, I will make here three tents, for you one and for Moses one and for Elijah one.

en.L: And Peter answered and said to Jesus, "Lord, it is good for us to be here. If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} wish, I will make three tents here, one for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} and one for Moses and one for Elijah."
en.B: Peter spoke up and said to Jesus, "Lord, how good it is that we are here! If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want, I will put up three shelters here: one for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, one for Moses, and one for Elijah."
en.R: Peter said to Jesus, "Lord, it is good for us to be here. If {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want, I will make three shelters here. One will be for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, one for Moses, and one for Elijah."

decisions.choice: answered: spoke up, though no question was asked
decisions.reason: The word often simply introduces what someone says in response to a situation.

decisions.choice: tents: shelters, such as huts of branches
decisions.reason: The word means a tent or booth. Israel lived in such shelters at the Festival of Booths (Leviticus 23:42-43), and God met Moses in a tent (Exodus 33:7-11). Matthew does not say what Peter had in mind; he seems to want to keep the moment and the visitors there.

decisions.choice: I will make, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: let us make, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "let us make", as in Mark 9:5 and Luke 9:33. The SBLGNT reads "I will make". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Lord: an address of respect and faith
decisions.reason: As in 8:25 and 16:22, Peter addresses Jesus as his Lord.

decisions.choice: shelters
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use a word for a simple temporary structure, as in Mark 9:5.

source.text: ἔτι αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος ἰδοὺ νεφέλη φωτεινὴ ἐπεσκίασεν αὐτούς, καὶ ἰδοὺ φωνὴ ἐκ τῆς νεφέλης λέγουσα· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἐν ᾧ εὐδόκησα· ἀκούετε αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Still him speaking behold, a cloud bright overshadowed them, and behold, a voice out of the cloud saying, This is the Son of me the beloved, in whom I was well pleased; listen to him.

en.L: While he was still speaking, look, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and look, a voice out of the cloud, saying, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Son, the beloved, in whom I am well pleased; listen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.B: Peter was still speaking when a cloud full of light covered them with its shadow, and a voice from the cloud said, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} dearly loved Son, and I delight in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Listen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."
en.R: While Peter was still talking, a bright cloud covered them like a shadow. A voice came from the cloud and said, "This is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Son, and I love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. I am very pleased with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Listen to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!"

decisions.choice: the bright cloud: the cloud of God's presence
decisions.reason: God came down in a cloud on Sinai and filled the tent of meeting with a cloud and his glory (Exodus 24:15-18; 40:34-35). The voice comes from the cloud, so the speaker is God.

decisions.choice: This is my Son, the beloved, in whom I am well pleased: the words spoken at Jesus's baptism (3:17)
decisions.reason: The voice repeats word for word what it said at the baptism, recalling Psalm 2:7 and Isaiah 42:1. As there, it tells those present who Jesus is.

decisions.choice: listen to him: the prophet like Moses
alternatives: a general call to pay attention
decisions.reason: Moses said that God would raise up a prophet like him, and Israel must listen to him (Deuteronomy 18:15). With Moses himself present, the voice points the disciples to Jesus.

decisions.choice: overshadowed them: covered them, perhaps all on the mountain
decisions.reason: "Them" may mean Jesus with Moses and Elijah, or the disciples too. The disciples' fear in 17:6 suggests they were inside the cloud or close to it.

decisions.choice: look (L, twice); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: my dearly loved Son, and I delight in him (B); my Son, and I love him. I am very pleased with him (R)
alternatives: my Son, the beloved, in whom I am well pleased
decisions.reason: The same renderings as at 3:17, so the reader hears the same words again.

decisions.choice: Peter
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker who is interrupted.

source.text: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ μαθηταὶ ἔπεσαν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον αὐτῶν καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν σφόδρα.

records.literal_gloss: And having heard the disciples fell on face of them and were afraid greatly.

en.L: And when the disciples heard [this], they fell on their faces and were exceedingly afraid.
en.B: Hearing the voice, the disciples fell face down on the ground in great fear.
en.R: The followers heard the voice. They were so afraid that they fell down with their faces to the ground.

decisions.choice: fell on their faces: bowing low before God's presence
decisions.reason: People in Scripture fall on their faces when God appears or speaks (Ezekiel 1:28; Daniel 8:17).

decisions.choice: were exceedingly afraid: terror before the holy God
decisions.reason: The disciples have heard God's own voice. Their fear is the dread of sinful people before God's holiness, which Jesus answers in 17:7.

decisions.choice: the voice
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the disciples heard.

source.text: καὶ προσῆλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ ἁψάμενος αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Ἐγέρθητε καὶ μὴ φοβεῖσθε.

records.literal_gloss: And came to [them] the Jesus and having touched them said, Rise and not be afraid.

en.L: And Jesus came to [them], and touching them said, "Get up, and do not be afraid."
en.B: Then Jesus came over, laid {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand on them, and said, "Get up, and stop being afraid."
en.R: Jesus came to them and touched them. He said, "Stand up. You do not need to be afraid."

decisions.choice: do not be afraid: stop being afraid
decisions.reason: The present tense with "not" tells them to stop what they are doing. Jesus calms the fear the voice caused (compare 14:27; 28:10).

decisions.choice: get up: rise from where they lay
decisions.reason: The disciples are lying face down (17:6). The same verb is used of Jesus being raised from the dead (17:9, 23).

decisions.choice: laid his hand on them
decisions.reason: Balanced describes the touch as a gesture of comfort.

source.text: ἐπάραντες δὲ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν οὐδένα εἶδον εἰ μὴ αὐτὸν Ἰησοῦν μόνον.

records.literal_gloss: Having lifted up and the eyes of them no one they saw except himself Jesus alone.

en.L: And lifting up their eyes, they saw no one except Jesus {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} alone.
en.B: When they raised their eyes, they saw no one there but Jesus alone.
en.R: When they looked up, they saw only Jesus. No one else was there.

decisions.choice: Jesus himself alone: Moses and Elijah are gone and Jesus remains
decisions.reason: The voice has just said "listen to him" (17:5). When the vision ends, Jesus is the one left for them to hear.

decisions.choice: not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Alone" and "only" already carry the stress of the word.

source.text: Καὶ καταβαινόντων αὐτῶν ἐκ τοῦ ὄρους ἐνετείλατο αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Μηδενὶ εἴπητε τὸ ὅραμα ἕως οὗ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐκ νεκρῶν ἐγερθῇ.

records.literal_gloss: And coming down they from the mountain commanded them the Jesus saying, To no one tell the vision until the Son of the Man out of dead is raised.

en.L: And as they were coming down from the mountain, Jesus commanded them, saying, "Tell the vision to no one until the Son of Man is raised from [the] dead."
en.B: On the way down the mountain Jesus gave them this order: "Tell no one about the vision until the Son of Man has been raised from the dead."
en.R: As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus gave them a command. He said, "Do not tell anyone what you saw until the Son of Man has been raised from death."

decisions.choice: the vision: what they saw, given by God
decisions.reason: The word means something seen. It is used of what God shows people, as of Moses at the burning bush (Acts 7:31). It does not suggest that the scene was unreal.

decisions.choice: is raised: a passive; God raises him
decisions.reason: The passive points to God's action, as in 16:21.

decisions.choice: tell no one: until the resurrection shows who he is
decisions.reason: Jesus has just begun to speak of his death and raising (16:21). Until then, what the disciples saw could be taken for the glory of an earthly king. After he is raised it can be told.

decisions.choice: what you saw
decisions.reason: Readable says what the vision was without suggesting a dream.

source.text: καὶ ἐπηρώτησαν αὐτὸν οἱ μαθηταὶ λέγοντες· Τί οὖν οἱ γραμματεῖς λέγουσιν ὅτι Ἠλίαν δεῖ ἐλθεῖν πρῶτον;

records.literal_gloss: And asked him the disciples saying, Why then the scribes say that Elijah it is necessary to come first?

en.L: And the disciples asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?"
en.B: So the disciples questioned {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}: "If that is so, why do the scribes say that Elijah has to come first?"
en.R: Then the followers asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Why do the teachers of the law say that Elijah has to come first?"

decisions.choice: Elijah must come first: Malachi 4:5
alternatives: a teaching of the scribes alone
decisions.reason: God promised to send Elijah the prophet before the great day of the LORD (Malachi 4:5; 3:23 in the Hebrew). The scribes taught from this that Elijah would come before the end.

decisions.choice: then: the question follows from what they have just seen and heard
decisions.reason: Elijah has appeared and gone, and Jesus speaks of his own death and raising. The disciples ask how this fits with Elijah coming first.

decisions.choice: If that is so
decisions.reason: Balanced spells out the link the word makes.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ἠλίας μὲν ἔρχεται καὶ ἀποκαταστήσει πάντα·

records.literal_gloss: He and answering said, Elijah indeed comes and will restore all things;

en.L: He answered and said, "Elijah does come, and he will restore all things.
en.B: He answered, "Elijah is indeed coming, and he will set all things right.
en.R: Jesus answered, "It is true that Elijah is coming. He will make everything right again.

decisions.choice: restore all things: Malachi 4:6
decisions.reason: Malachi says the coming Elijah will turn the hearts of fathers to their children and children to their fathers (Malachi 4:6; 3:24 in the Hebrew).

decisions.choice: Elijah does come: Jesus agrees with the scribes' teaching
alternatives: Elijah is still to come in the future
decisions.reason: Jesus grants what the scribes say and then shows in 17:12 how it has been fulfilled. The present "comes" states the teaching; it does not mean a second coming of Elijah after John.

decisions.choice: is coming, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: is coming first, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "first", as in Mark 9:12. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

source.text: λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι Ἠλίας ἤδη ἦλθεν, καὶ οὐκ ἐπέγνωσαν αὐτὸν ἀλλὰ ἐποίησαν ἐν αὐτῷ ὅσα ἠθέλησαν· οὕτως καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου μέλλει πάσχειν ὑπ’ αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: I say but to you that Elijah already came, and not they recognized him but did to him whatever they wanted; so also the Son of the Man is about to suffer by them.

en.L: But I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they wished; so also the Son of Man is about to suffer at their hands."
en.B: But I tell you that Elijah has come already. They did not recognize him, and they treated him however they pleased. They will make the Son of Man suffer in the same way."
en.R: But I tell you, Elijah has already come. People did not know who he was. They did whatever they wanted to him. In the same way, they will make the Son of Man suffer."

decisions.choice: did to him whatever they wished: John was imprisoned and killed
decisions.reason: Herod Antipas put John in prison and had him beheaded (14:3-12). "They" takes in Herod and the leaders who rejected John (21:25-32).

decisions.choice: so also the Son of Man: the forerunner's fate shows what awaits Jesus
decisions.reason: The one who prepared the way was rejected and killed; the one he prepared for will be treated the same (16:21).

decisions.choice: is about to: soon, and as God has planned
decisions.reason: The verb speaks of what is going to happen, and soon, as in 17:22.

decisions.choice: They will make the Son of Man suffer
alternatives: the Son of Man is about to suffer at their hands
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the passive idea into an active sentence with "they" as subject.

source.text: τότε συνῆκαν οἱ μαθηταὶ ὅτι περὶ Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: Then understood the disciples that concerning John the Baptist he spoke to them.

en.L: Then the disciples understood that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had spoken to them about John the Baptist.
en.B: The disciples then realized that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} meant John the Baptist.
en.R: Then the followers understood. Jesus was talking about John the Baptist.

decisions.choice: John the Baptist: the Elijah who was to come
decisions.reason: Jesus has already said that John is the Elijah who was to come (11:14). John came in Elijah's role, not as Elijah reborn (Luke 1:17; John 1:21).

decisions.choice: meant
decisions.reason: Balanced puts it briefly: they saw whom his words were about.
